messages:
Maya Patel: Hey all — quick question from my first week. When I have setup issues (VPN, laptop, dev creds), where should I post? Also there are a bunch of silly bots in other channels — which bots are safe to interact with vs which I should avoid?
Alex Chen: Welcome, Maya! For infra/setup stuff, post in #help first — folks there triage and point you to the right owner. If it’s urgent (can't access prod or VPN), ping @samir or @eng-oncall. :wave:
Jen Ortega: For laptop/IT requests use the ticket link in the pinned messages in #people-ops — that creates a ticket instead of spamming a channel. For creds, never post secrets in channels, always DM or use the secrets onboarding form.
Samir Rao: Re bots — the handful we use frequently are: Onboarding Bot (gives checklist), DeployBot (deploy notifications, do NOT run it unless you know the flow), and PagerBot (pages on-call). You can interact with Onboarding Bot freely to mark tasks done. Avoid trying slash commands from unknown bots in public channels.
Maya Patel: Got it — is there a short etiquette checklist for channel posting? I don’t want to clog #general with dumb questions.
Alex Chen: Short version: 1) Search first (Slack search + handbook). 2) Post in the channel most relevant (see pinned channel-usage guide). 3) Keep posts explicit (what you tried, short logs). 4) Use threads to keep the channel tidy. 5) Escalate to DMs or @mentions when it’s blocking your day.
Jen Ortega: Examples: for "my build fails" — post in #eng with a short code block: ```
make build
./bin/foo: permission denied
``` and say what os and machine. For "how to request laptop" — #people-ops. For infra access — #eng-infra.
Onboarding Bot: Hi Maya! To retrigger your onboarding checklist type: `/onboard me` — the bot will DM you steps and links. Use `/onboard status` to see remaining items.
Samir Rao: Also, if you need to test a bot command, consider doing it in your DM with the bot or in #devex-sandbox (we have a small channel for safe bot experimentation).
Maya Patel: Perfect, thanks. One more: what about posting logs or stack traces — should I paste or attach as a gist?
Alex Chen: If it's short (<10 lines) paste in a fenced code block. For long traces, create a private gist or pastebin and link it (make it unlisted), or attach as a file. Mark logs with the minimal repro steps.
Jen Ortega: And if you accidentally post a secret — delete the message and notify security (@security). We have a secrets-rotation playbook pinned in #eng-security.
Maya Patel: Thanks y’all — this helps a lot. I'll use #help first and the sandbox channel for bot testing. :thumbsup:
Samir Rao: One last operational note: some integrations post HIPAA/PCI-sensitive alerts in private channels only — don’t invite external contractors to those channels. If you're unsure, ask #security.
Alex Chen: +1 — welcome again, and ping any of us if anything blocks you.
Maya Patel: Appreciate it!
